title: Affine elementary etale finite-over-smooth local structure
statement: Let $p:Z\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $z\in Z$, put $s=p(z)$, and let $n=\dim_z(Z_s)$ for $Z_s=Z\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field, def-kun-dimension]. There exist affine schemes $W,Y,S_1$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], points $w\in W$, $y\in Y$, $s_1\in S_1$, and morphisms $b:W\to Z$, $a:S_1\to S$, $\pi:W\to Y$, $h:Y\to S_1$ with $pb=ah\pi$, $b(w)=z$, $\pi(w)=y$, and $h(y)=s_1$, such that $b$ and $a$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and induce isomorphisms $\kappa(z)\cong\kappa(w)$ and $\kappa(s)\cong\kappa(s_1)$, $\pi$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and $\pi^{-1}(\{y\})=\{w\}$, and $h$ is smooth of relative dimension $n$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with geometrically integral fibres. Geometrically integral means that each fibre remains integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] after every extension of its residue field. Moreover $\kappa(y)/\kappa(s_1)$ is purely transcendental, meaning isomorphic over $\kappa(s_1)$ to a rational function field $\kappa(s_1)(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$ in algebraically independent variables for some $r\ge0$.

source.place: Tags 057K and 057L, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type, clauses (1)--(6), and lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type-affine, clause (7).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-smooth-preliminary-chart] to $p,z,n$. Obtain an affine open $j:S_0\hookrightarrow S$, the marked diagram $W_0\xrightarrow{\pi_0}Y_0\xrightarrow{h_0}S_0$, and $b_0:W_0\to Z$. This supplies finite $\pi_0$ with singleton marked fibre, elementary etale $b_0$, affine $Y_0,S_0$, finite presentation and relative dimension $n$ for $h_0$, and the purely transcendental marked residue extension. Its marked equations are $b_0(w_0)=z$, $\pi_0(w_0)=y_0$, $h_0(y_0)=s_0$, $j(s_0)=s$, and $pb_0=jh_0\pi_0$.

source.place: Tag 052E, lemma-local-structure-finite-type, proof; Tag 057K, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type, proof through the affine choice of Y and finite presentation of h.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-smooth-integral-base-refinement] to $\pi_0,h_0,w_0$. Its affine, finite-presentation, smooth-dimension, rational-residue-extension and singleton-fibre hypotheses all come from step 1. Write $e:S_1\to S_0$, $v:V\to Y_0$, $\rho:W_1\to W_0$, $\pi_1:W_1\to V$, and $h_1:V\to S_1$ for its output. Set $b_1=b_0\rho$ and $a_1=je$. The open immersion $j$ and these etale maps compose to make $b_1,a_1$ etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The marked residue maps are $\kappa(z)\to\kappa(w_0)\to\kappa(w_1)$ and $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(s_0)\to\kappa(s_1)$; each arrow is an isomorphism, the one for $j$ being the identical local ring on its open neighbourhood. From $h_0v=eh_1$ and $\pi_0\rho=v\pi_1$ we get $pb_1=jh_0\pi_0\rho=jeh_1\pi_1=a_1h_1\pi_1$. The refinement gives $e(s_1)=s_0$, $\rho(w_1)=w_0$, $\pi_1(w_1)=y_1$, $h_1(y_1)=s_1$, so $b_1(w_1)=z$ and $a_1(s_1)=s$. It also supplies the singleton fibre, geometric integrality, relative dimension $n$ and purely transcendental residue extension.

source.place: Tag 057K, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type, proof from the connected component T through the outer pullback diagram and the marked residue-field identifications.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-marked-finite-smooth-affine-refinement] to $W_1\xrightarrow{\pi_1}V\xrightarrow{h_1}S_1,w_1$; step 2 supplies finiteness, singleton fibre, smooth relative dimension $n$ and geometrically integral fibres. Let $U,Y,W$ be its affine output, with inclusions $i_U,i_Y,i_W$ and marked points $s_1,y,w$. Put $a=a_1i_U$, $b=b_1i_W$ and use its restricted maps $\pi,h$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], these composites are etale. The inclusions induce the residue-field identifications stated by the refinement, so both marked residue isomorphisms and the rational function extension persist. Its equations yield $pb=pb_1i_W=a_1h_1\pi_1i_W=a_1i_Uh\pi=ah\pi$. Since the inclusions preserve the marked points, $b(w)=z$, $\pi(w)=y$ and $h(y)=s_1$. Its conclusion supplies finiteness, singleton fibre, relative dimension $n$ and geometric integrality; rename $U$ as the final $S_1$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_affine_etale_finite_smooth_local_structure {Z S : Scheme.{u}} (p : Z ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType p] (z : Z) : ∃ (n : ℕ), topologicalKrullDimAt (p.asFiber z) = (n : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ ∃ (W Y S₁ : Scheme.{u}) (w : W) (y : Y) (s₁ : S₁) (b : W ⟶ Z) (a : S₁ ⟶ S) (π : W ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ S₁), IsAffine W ∧ IsAffine Y ∧ IsAffine S₁ ∧ b w = z ∧ π w = y ∧ h y = s₁ ∧ b ≫ p = π ≫ h ≫ a ∧ Etale b ∧ Etale a ∧ IsIso (b.residueFieldMap w) ∧ IsIso (a.residueFieldMap s₁) ∧ IsFinite π ∧ π ⁻¹' ({y} : Set Y) = ({w} : Set W) ∧ SmoothOfRelativeDimension n h ∧ GeometricallyIntegral h ∧ @Algebra.IsPurelyTranscendentalExtension (S₁.residueField (h y)) (Y.residueField y) _ _ ((h.residueFieldMap y).hom.toAlgebra)
